title: Having Something Done (-tat/-tet Causatives)
goal: I can form causative verbs using -at/-et and -tat/-tet according to syllable count and stem structure
I can apply vowel harmony accurately across back-vowel and front-vowel causative stems

sections.title: Unit 10: Mentorship, Discipline & Intellectual Growth
body: Hungary's legendary secondary schools and university seminars—from the classical gymnasiums depicted by Mihály Babits and Géza Ottlik to modern research workshops—were built on demanding mentorship. Describing how a teacher challenges students, commissions translations, or makes scholars rethink their assumptions requires the Hungarian causative suffix system (-at/-et, -tat/-tet).

In this unit, you will master how syllable count and stem structure govern the choice between -at/-et and -tat/-tet, how Hungarian assigns cases when a third participant enters the clause (-val/-vel for the intermediate agent of a transitive verb versus -t for the causee of an intransitive verb), and how lexicalized causatives (tanít, épít) contrast with second-level productive causatives (taníttat, építtet).
